newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs close narrowly mixed, investor caution.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs close narrowly mixed, investor caution.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed narrowly mixed in low volume Monday as the economy's slower-than-expected growth has made investors reluctant to enter the market, brokers said.
A similar overall trend was likely Tuesday, but individual stocks could see variations as third quarter financial results were published, they added.
Monday, the General Index edged down 0.06 percent to 1,567.13 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 0.20 percent to 2,122.48 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
In a total of 1,776 trades, 29 stocks fell, 28 rose and 21 were stable in volume of 17.5 million ($6.8 million).

"Foreign investors were cautious. They have been trading very selectively since the release (on October 7) of the August (year-on-year) gross domestic product growth (GDP) figure of 1.8 percent," said Arnaldo Fiorani of local brokerage Interfip, adding the market had generally been expecting a higher GDP figure.
The Peruvian economy grew 2.0 percent in the first eight months of the year, compared with 8.4 percent in the same period of 1995, according to the government.

While investors recognized as prudent the government's policy of slowing the economy down at the beginning of the year, they had been hoping for a quicker recovery in the second half than has so far been seen, brokers said.
The government is predicting annual growth of between three and four percent in 1996, down from initial projections of between five and six percent.
Monday, benchmark Telefonica del Peru accounted for 29 percent of the market's volume as it rose 0.53 percent to 5.70 soles.

Among other leaders, tin-miner Minsur - the one blue-chip stock to have its third quarter financial results published Monday -- was the second most heavily traded stock as it rose 1.42 percent to 25.00 soles in 18 percent of the day's volume.
The miner announced its January to September net rose 4.7 percent to 79.4 million soles, compared to the same period the previous year.
Brewery Compania Nacional de Cerveza, closed up 1.31 percent at 1.55 soles in six percent of the day's volume.
